2608.05266.title: Agentic self-driving microscopy benchmarks support qualification but do not necessarily generalize to unseen tasks
2608.05266.paper_summary: Large language model agents are increasingly being developed to control a wide range of scientific characterization tools including microscopes and synchrotron beamlines. Research into agentic control of physical infrastructure is nascent and there are few well-established paradigms for how to engineer an agentic system. There are many choices to make when designing a microscopy agent, including the choice of LLM, the number of agents to use, agent responsibilities and delegation rules, retrieval-augmented generation parameters, and more. When designing and optimizing an agentic microscope controller, researchers not only want to ensure that the agent can correctly perform known tasks but also that the agent can generalize to new tasks that it has not encountered before. In this study, we develop a benchmark and trace-logging framework that reveals a) how different choices of agent architecture impact performance at microscopy tasks and b) the limitations of benchmarks for predicting if a particular agent will perform well on unseen microscopy tasks. The framework was used to evaluate one-, two-, and three-agent graph topologies, five LLMs, RAG and context parameters, and operational constraints across 53 microscopy benchmark tests. In total, 105 agent configurations, 1,949 individual test runs, and 49,109 RAG retrievals were recorded. Direct comparisons showed clear differences in latency, token use, cost, and failure mode between configurations. However, surrogate models trained on agent architecture and test results did not reliably predict an agent's performance on new, unseen tasks. These results show that these benchmarks are useful for qualification, regression testing, diagnosis, and direct comparison, but the current heterogeneous test suite does not support a task-independent global configuration model.
2608.05266.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型代理正越來越多地被開發用於控制各種科學表徵工具，包括顯微鏡和同步輻射光束線。對於物理基礎設施的代理控制的研究尚處於起步階段，並且對於如何設計一個代理系統的成熟範式仍然很少。設計顯微鏡代理時有許多選擇需要考慮，包括LLM的選擇、使用的代理數量、代理的職責和委派規則、檢索增強生成參數等。在設計和優化代理顯微鏡控制器時，研究人員不僅希望確保代理能正確執行已知任務，還希望代理能夠對未遇到的新任務進行泛化。在本研究中，我們開發了一個基準和追蹤日誌框架，揭示了a) 不同的代理架構選擇如何影響顯微鏡任務的性能，以及b) 基準在預測特定代理在未見顯微鏡任務上的表現方面的局限性。該框架用於評估一、二和三代理的圖形拓撲、五種LLM、RAG和上下文參數，以及53個顯微鏡基準測試中的操作約束。總共記錄了105個代理配置、1,949個單獨測試運行和49,109次RAG檢索。直接比較顯示配置之間在延遲、標記使用、成本和失敗模式上存在明顯差異。然而，基於代理架構和測試結果訓練的替代模型並未可靠地預測代理在新的、未見任務上的表現。這些結果表明，這些基準對於資格認證、回歸測試、診斷和直接比較是有用的，但當前的異質測試套件不支持任務獨立的全局配置模型。
